study.question: Does the click-AUC loss after reducing the context-owning buy tower from [112,64] to [96,48] depend primarily on its first hidden width, its second hidden width, or their interaction, and can either isolated reduction lower measured prediction cost while preserving click AUC?
study.hypothesis: Marginal capacity utility is layer-specific in the buy head that supplies auxiliary gradients to shared context. The second hidden representation may carry the useful context-gradient signal, while some first-layer channels may be dispensable. This is unverified. Earlier coupled reduction changes both layers and initialization scale correction only partially recovers its click AUC; neither observation establishes which layer matters. A prospective 2x2 factorial at inherited weight scale can identify the operational layer-width dependence under this recipe. It cannot prove why gradients differ or establish equal-capacity superiority.

nearest_work.difference: Archived primary text inspected at lines260-335: target-conditioned unnormalized activation pooling and Dice are inherited, adapted to four labels and compressed field/action histories. This proposal changes only two buy tower widths within the existing local model; no new pooling, Dice, unified architecture, or priority claim.

Pinned reset_parameters uses Xavier-normal Linear weights and zero biases. Retain the same full-template draw order and inherited slice scale to isolate width policies, rather than adopting a new training recipe.

Pinned Dice has per-channel alpha and non-affine BatchNorm. The inherited reduction helper physically slices alpha and running statistics with the layer channels. No change to Dice equations or training populations.

Resolved primary provenance and attempted bounded read; detailed text is unavailable. The explicit unirank-benchmark-v2 fallback describes hub-mediated task/field/sequence interaction. None is adopted; no original-method reproduction or novelty comparison is claimed.

This exact standalone source and its executable methods are inherited. Two previously coupled buy hidden widths become independent factorial factors; all other modules, losses and gradient-ownership rules remain fixed.

study.proposed_difference: A 2x2 architecture factorial: buy first hidden width112 versus96, crossed with second hidden width64 versus48, always using inherited retained-weight scale. New cells [96,64] and [112,48] separate the previously coupled removal. Fresh [112,64] and [96,48] controls reproduce the previous endpoints and provide contemporaneous cost measurements. Existing constructor support implements this through explicit CONFIG overrides; no executable method is changed. This is a local capacity attribution study, not a new architectural contribution.
predictions: [96,64] is predicted to retain click AUC better than [112,48] despite removing more parameters, consistent with the second hidden representation having greater marginal utility. Equal or reversed ordering falsifies this directional prediction.

Full and combined controls should reproduce their same-protocol historical click AUCs 0.6671669182126774 and 0.6665210135841103 within numerical tolerance; deviations require execution diagnosis before interpreting new widths.

Expected dense parameters: reference204531, first-only197075, second-only202691, both195491; embeddings stay31793216. Formula for buy tower at input400: P(h1,h2)=402*h1+(h1+3)*h2+1. These are derived expectations pending host verification.
Report effects A=Q(96,64)-Q(112,64), B=Q(112,48)-Q(112,64), and interaction Q(96,48)-Q(96,64)-Q(112,48)+Q(112,64), with paired uncertainty where authorized predictions are available.

Prospective utility screening, applying only to these new runs: click AUC loss at most0.0001 against contemporaneous [112,64] AND at most0.0001 below historical incumbent0.6671669182126774; fewer measured Parameters; p50 model-only batch latency at least1% lower with p95 no more than1% higher and no worsening of whole-validation inference_seconds. A one-run pass is preliminary; final preservation requires paired user-cluster/bootstrap and seed comparisons where available. No changed threshold may be justified by these outcomes.
No auxiliary preservation is predicted. Report all task AUC/Logloss and auxiliary mean independently; the efficient parent already has much worse auxiliary AUC than the baseline.
falsifiers: A reproducible click-AUC loss greater than0.0001 or failure of measured prediction-cost criteria rejects that candidate utility under the frozen protocol, even if parameter count is lower.
If [96,64] does not retain more click AUC than [112,48], reject the directional second-layer-utility hypothesis for this implementation; this does not refute all layer allocations.
If both isolated cuts lose AUC comparably, or the combined loss is mostly additive without the predicted ordering, the proposed layer-specific explanation is unsupported.

If a control fails same-protocol reproduction (absolute click AUC deviation greater than0.00001), or any finite-output, mask, storage or ownership prerequisite fails, treat execution reliability separately from scientific counterevidence; do not select a candidate until diagnosed.
Lower parameter counts with unchanged or higher latency/validation inference time do not establish prediction-cost savings.
alternative_explanations: Layer widths remove unequal numbers of parameters and operations; this is not a capacity-matched allocation comparison.
Slicing changes functions and gradient magnitudes; retained template initialization scale and Dice statistics can interact with width.
Buy context gradients and global dense clipping can change shared updates; downstream AUC cannot isolate a unique gradient mechanism.
Single seed and one-pass training; repeated same-seed bridges do not establish independent support.
Small dense reductions are dominated by 31,793,216 embedding parameters and attention/loading costs; latency can be unchanged or noisy.
The large known auxiliary-task degradation may reflect changed auxiliary gradient usefulness rather than surplus representation capacity.
Prior rescaling shifted both full and reduced scores, so optimization geometry remains relevant even with retained scale frozen; no claim that initialization effects were excluded.
